title: 3 men face federal charges in Rochester-area cocaine trafficking bust

 Rochester, N.Y. — Three men from Monroe County face federal charges after authorities seized nearly 30 kilograms of cocaine, approximately $159,000 in cash and four guns as part of an investigation into an illegal drug trafficking operation, federal prosecutors announced Tuesday.
 In a release, U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo said 58-year-old Rodney Stanley of Greece, 36-year-old Leonardo Gaskin of Henrietta and 52-year-old Shanimba Nelson of Irondequoit were responsible for storing, packaging and distributing cocaine, and collecting payment for it, in the Rochester area.
 Gaskin's vehicle was seen traveling to the Philadelphia area Oct. 8, staying for about 15 minutes and returning overnight to his home, according to the release.
 Gaskin was observed making multiple, similar, quick-turnaround-trips to the New York, New York/Tri-State and Philadelphia, PA-areas, which are believed to be source locations for the organization’s cocaine. The release said authorities executed a search warrant at Gaskin's home and on his vehicle Oct. 9, seizing approximately 23 kilograms of suspected cocaine, three cellphones, $4,857 in cash and drug paraphernalia.
 A search warrant was also executed at a stash house on Plymouth Avenue in Rochester, which was frequented by Gaskin. Investigators recovered approximately 1.9 kilograms of cocaine, two firearms, approximately $84,685.00 in cash, and drug paraphernalia. Investigators also executed a search warrant at Nelson's home the same day, seizing approximately 146 grams of suspected crack cocaine and 3.677 kilograms of cocaine, along with $8,209 in cash, drug paraphernalia and a loaded shotgun, according to the release. 
 A search of Stanley's home the same day uncovered a loaded pistol, approximately 1.23 kilograms of cocaine and $51,129 in cash, according to the release.
 A search warrant was also executed at a suspected stash house on East Avenue in Rochester, which was frequented by Stanley. During that search, investigators recovered approximately 22 grams of crack cocaine, approximately 229 grams of bulk marijuana, approximately $10,255.00 in cash, and drug paraphernalia. Law enforcement also surveilled the house and observed Stanley entering and exiting the location and conducting narcotics transactions in a nearby parking lot. All three men were charged with possession with intent to distribute cocaine, according to the release. Nelson and Stanley were also charged with possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. Gaskin was held following a detention hearing, while Nelson and Stanley were released on conditions.
 "These defendants crossed state lines to secure multiple kilograms of cocaine, storing them in stash houses embedded in our residential neighborhoods before pushing the drugs onto our streets," DiGiacomo said in a statement. "Their arrests should send an unmistakable message: law enforcement at every level is fully unified and relentless in disrupting these operations and cutting off the flow of illegal narcotics into our community."
